precepts.text: There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God; their throat is an open sepulchre, with their tongues they have used deceit, the poison of asps is under their lips. This describes the same wicked mouths David speaks of in Psalm 5:9.
precepts.point: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue. The enemies are full of wickedness and deceit, flattering with their tongues.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

precepts.why:
Paul describes the same wicked mouths David speaks of: “There is none that understandeth, there is none that seeketh after God. They are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable; there is none that doeth good, no, not one.” Then he uses David's very words: “Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips”.

This is why David asks, “Lead me, O Lord, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies”. The enemies watching him have no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness, and they flatter with their tongue. What comes out of their throat is death, like an open grave, and deceit and poison sit under their lips. Because of enemies like that David needs the Most High to make his way straight before his face.

precepts.text: Look at how David operated: in all his works he praised the Most High with words of glory and loved Him that made him, and even through all the trials he went through the Lord took away his sins and exalted his horn forever. That is what you want, for the Most High to take away your sins.
precepts.point: For thou, Lord, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield. The Most High fights our battles as long as we align ourselves with these scriptures and keep the commandments, including the commandment of brotherly and sisterly love, which Israel sometimes forgets, especially in marriage. Sometimes you have to take an L in this walk.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

precepts.why:
Look at how David operated. “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.” He “played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs”, and while he was yet young he slew a giant and took away reproach from the people when he “beat down the boasting of Goliath”. How? “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior”. That is the Most High defending the one who put his trust in him, just as Psalm 5 says: “let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them”.

“For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his adversaries”. The Most High fights our battles as long as we align ourselves with these scriptures and keep the commandments, including the commandment of brotherly and sisterly love, which Israel sometimes forgets, especially in marriage. Sometimes you have to take an L in this walk.

“In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” He set singers before the altar, beautified the feasts and set in order the solemn times, that the temple might sound from morning. And through all the trials he went through, “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” That is what you want: for the Most High to take away your sins. That is how he blesses the righteous and compasses him with favour as with a shield.

precepts.text: The foolish shall not stand in his sight; God hates all workers of iniquity, and iniquity is sin.
precepts.point: The righteous are saved by being judged out of the book of life alongside the record of their works. Christianity is worse than crack cocaine because it tells our people to believe on Christ while keeping no commandments, setting them on the path to destruction.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
God “saveth the upright in heart”, and Psalm 5 shows the other side: “The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity.” Iniquity is sin. God hates all workers of sin, and the foolish shall not stand in his sight.

So the defence of God is for the upright in heart, the righteous. Those who keep believing on Christ while working iniquity, as Christianity teaches our people, are not the upright in heart; they are the workers of iniquity that God hates, and they will not stand in his sight.

points: Give ear to my words, O Lord, consider my meditation. Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my King and my God, for unto thee will I pray. David directs his cry to the Most High as his King and his God.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up. David sets his prayer before the Most High in the morning and looks up in expectation.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: For thou art not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness, neither shall evil dwell with thee. The foolish shall not stand in thy sight; thou hatest all workers of iniquity. The Most High hates all workers of iniquity.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing (lying); the Lord will abhor the bloody and deceitful man. The Most High will destroy the liar and abhors the bloody and deceitful.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: But as for me, I will come into thy house in the multitude of thy mercy, and in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple. David sets himself apart from the wicked, coming into the Most High's house in reverence.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: Lead me, O Lord, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies; make thy way straight before my face. David asks to be led in righteousness because of the enemies watching him.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: For there is no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part is very wickedness; their throat is an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue. The enemies are full of wickedness and deceit, flattering with their tongues.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: Destroy thou them, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; cast them out in the multitude of their transgressions, for they have rebelled against thee. David asks that the wicked fall by their own schemes because they rebelled against the Most High.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

points: But let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice; let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them; let them also that love thy name be joyful in thee. The Most High defends those who trust in Him, just as He defended David.
